To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
herbivory on temperate rainforest seedlings in sun and shade is mediated by differential resistance, tolerance, and herbivore abundance.
1) herbivy pressure was greater in the sun, 2) shade plants were less resistant, 3) shade plants were more susceptible to herbivory damage, and 4) sun plants were more tolerant to herbivory.
herbivory may contribute significantly to the exclusion of light-demanding tree seedlings from shade habitats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of herbivory on the establishment and distribution of a light-demanding species in a temperate forest.
the effects of herbivory on plant performance and distribution, and the role of plant traits (e.g., resistance, tolerance) as determinants of herbivore damage.
the effects of herbivory on plant establishment in contrasting habitats and how herbivory can contribute to the maintenance of the light gradient.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
herbivore pressure and plant resistance and/or tolerance to herbivory may contribute, in a complex way, to the distribution of plants along the light gradient.
herbivory in temperate rainforests is more important for the light-demanding species than for shade-tolerant ones.
herbivory is a major factor influencing plant distribution along the sun/shade gradient, but its relative importance depends on the specific plant-herbivore interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
herbivory is a significant factor in the distribution of a tree species in a temperate forest along the light gradient.
herbivore pressure on seedlings of light-demanding tree is greater in the sun than in the shade, due to greater abundance of herbivores in sun and greater resistance of shade plants.
herbivory on E. coccinenum seedlings is greater in the sun, and that the consequences of herbivory are more detrimental in shade, where plants are less resistant and less tolerant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
herbivory may be an important factor in the establishment and distribution of light-demanding plant species in the shade.

herbivory may be a significant factor in determining the distribution of plant species along the light gradient, and that the relative importance of herbivory in determining plant distribution may vary among plant species and light environments.
the differential herbivory and plant resistance or tolerance along a light gradient can contribute to the exclusion or maintenance of a plant species along a light gradient.
